title: The Role of Model Confidence on Bias Effects in Measured Uncertainties for Vision-Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model sensitivity to arbitrary linguistic choices by rephrasing prompts while preserving the underlying semantic meaning.
Measuring the model's preference for certain option locations by shuffling the positions of input options in multiple-choice formats.
Assessing the model's reliance on specific token assignments by shuffling the categorical labels (e.g., 0, 1, 2, 3) assigned to the options.
Testing vision-language models' reliance on shape cues by intentionally distorting the shapes of objects through resizing images with varying length-to-width ratios.
Evaluating the effect of image orientation on model predictions by rotating input images by varying degrees (e.g., -45° to 45°).
Measuring the model's reliance on low-level visual features like texture and lighting by injecting random Gaussian noise into the images to disrupt local features.
